name: Deciding fast in fast markets
idea: The work argues that firms which make strategic decisions quickly in fast-changing industries do not do so by cutting back on information or options. They use up-to-date information about how the business is running, weigh several alternatives at the same time, and lean on advisers with relevant experience.
suggests: Look at how the company decides when its market moves quickly: what information it uses day to day, how many options it keeps open at once, and whom it asks for advice.
limits: The work is about decisions in industries that change quickly, so what it argues is tied to that kind of setting.
competing_idea: The work sets its account against the common view that deciding fast means doing less analysis, a view in which thorough and slower analysis is what leads to better decisions.
questions: What information does the company use when it must decide quickly, and how current is it?
How many alternatives does the company keep open at once when it decides under time pressure?
Who advises on fast decisions, and what experience do they bring?

originals.reference: K. M. Eisenhardt, "Making Fast Strategic Decisions in High-Velocity Environments", Academy of Management Journal, Vol. 32 No. 3, 1989, pp. 543-576
